messages:
maria: Heads-up — I'm worried about bulk delta sync + fallback to full seed during peak egress. If a site falls back we could accidentally saturate their link and make all apps unhappy. Need a plan for throttling + prioritized resume.
jason: +1. My quick take: token-bucket policer per-site with a global soft cap. If we detect fallback to full-seed, switch to serialized download mode with exponential backoff between shards.
sasha: Can we stream ordered shards and apply-in-place so we don't need full-seed often? Operator UX is the tricky part (how do they surface priority)?
infra-bot: Build artifact 6143217777 published: delta-index v2. CI link: https://ci.redwood.internal/artifacts/6143217777 (checksums attached) :package:
ryan: Throttling is good but beware of apply timeouts. If we serialize too much, operator will see long apply durations and abort, which leads to more retries. We should expose adaptive concurrency: bump concurrency when apply lag < threshold.
kevin: Also consider checksum-first prefetch: fetch only missing shards based on manifest checksums. I think the proto supports it but operator signals are missing.
maria: Agree. Minimal operator flags I'd like: `--prefetch-priority=critical|background` and `--egress-policer=token_bucket:RATE` so site admins can set limits.
jason: Example config sketch:
```yaml
egress:
  policer:
    type: token_bucket
    rate: 10mbps
    burst: 2mb
  fallback:
    mode: serialized
    backoff: 2s
```
sasha: Edge-case: network flaps during serialized fallback — resume tokens need to be idempotent and manifest versions must be immutable. We should add manifest version + chunk-id stable hashing to guarantee resume compatibility.
ryan: Also add metrics/alerts: `packaging.egress.bytes`, `packaging.apply.lag_seconds`, and an SLO alert when apply_lag > 300s for > 2 nodes.
maria: I'll draft RFC for: (1) rate-limiting policy, (2) operator flags, (3) manifest/chunk id stability, (4) metrics. Assigning @jason for policer impl and @sasha for manifest schema changes. :memo: :white_check_mark:
jason: I'll take policing. Quick question: per-cluster default or per-operator? I'm leaning per-cluster default with operator override.
sasha: Per-cluster default + per-operator override sounds right. Operator-level setting for edge customers.
infra-bot: Reminder: Packaging team sync at 09:30 tomorrow to triage perf and RFC action items.
maria: Thanks all — I'll post a short RFC draft in #architecture tomorrow morning and tag you both.
